clue.text: Got up for the occasion, like My Lady Nicotine ?

definitions.meaning: prepared and settled beforehand, arranged in advance
My Lady Nicotine is J. M. Barrie's book in praise of tobacco, and pipe tobacco is sold chopped and cured

explanation.surface: Someone dressed up for a party is compared to Barrie's tobacco-loving book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up' suggests dressing up, but here it means arranged beforehand; the second sense is literal, as tobacco leaf is sliced and cured.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter fixed in advance is settled with no room for change; tobacco is literally sliced and cured.

definitions.meaning: to dock is to cut short, as with a tail or wages
cynosure comes from Greek for a dog's tail, the old name of the Pole Star's constellation

explanation.surface: Harbours are described as centres of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docks' looks like a noun for harbours; it is the verb meaning shortens. A cur is a dog, so a cur's tail is the literal Greek sense of cynosure.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock is to shorten; a cynosure is etymologically a dog's tail, broken up as mongrel plus rear appendages.

parts.note: the New York district of songwriters and music publishers, home of American popular music

explanation.surface: Father is said to have a favourite spot across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' reads as Dad, but it means popular music; its haunt across the Atlantic is the American songwriting quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York district of music publishers was the centre of American popular song writing.

clue.text: Recesses to be measured in inches

indicators.note: the word inches is measured out again, its letters laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: Alcoves are to be sized up using an inch scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'measured' rearranges INCHES; 'to be' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Niches are hollows set into walls, the same as small recesses or alcoves.

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medico
single means one

explanation.surface: A doctor living alone is described as an idler.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male bee that does no work, hence an idle person who lives off others.

parts.note: read as describing something that gratifies wishes freely, giving in to every whim

explanation.surface: An exclamation of pleasure at something satisfying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gratifying' reads as pleasing to receive, but it means granting others what they want, as a lenient parent does.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lenient grants every wish, so is very much given to pleasing others' desires.

parts.note: the Twins of the zodiac are Castor and Pollux, known by another collective name in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A star sign is said to go under an assumed name.
explanation.walkthrough: Gemini, the Twins, are Castor and Pollux, called by a Greek name meaning sons of Zeus.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor and Pollux, the heavenly twins of the zodiac, are known collectively by this Greek title meaning sons of Zeus.

clue.text: Bracing brain and sinew; Blow thou wind of —- " (Kingsley)

definitions.text: Bracing brain and sinew; Blow thou wind of —- " (Kingsley)

parts.words: Bracing brain and sinew; Blow thou wind of —- " (Kingsley)
parts.note: a line from Charles Kingsley's Ode to the North-East Wind, whose missing last word names the deity

explanation.surface: A quotation from Kingsley's poem praising the bracing north-east wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley's Ode to the North-East Wind closes its stanza calling the wind that of the Almighty.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley's line reads 'Blow, thou wind of' followed by the word for the Almighty.

explanation.surface: A dramatist is described as in good spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: John Gay (1685-1732) wrote The Beggar's Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The old sense is merry or light-hearted; John Gay was the author of The Beggar's Opera.

parts.note: Antic Hay is Aldous Huxley's novel, but a hay is an old country round, and an antic one a lively example

explanation.surface: Huxley's novel is offered as an example of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The title looks like it wants a novel; a hay is a country dance with weaving figures, and antic means grotesque or capering.
explanation.definitionFit: A hay is a rustic round with interweaving figures, so an antic hay is a kind of jig or reel.

clue.text: This ancient character is heard to regret the devil

indicators.note: the clue says the phrase is heard, so the letters entered sound like it rather than spell it

parts.note: to rue is to regret, and Old Nick is the devil

explanation.surface: An ancient person is overheard repenting dealings with Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is heard' tells you RUE NICK said aloud gives the answer; 'character' means a letter, as in old Germanic script, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes are the letters of the old Germanic alphabets, so a runic character is an ancient written letter.

parts.note: the eldest patriarch of Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga, named to distinguish him from younger namesakes

explanation.surface: An elderly teller of Norse tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Saga suggests Norse legend, but it is The Forsyte Saga, where the patriarch is distinguished from his son and grandson of the same first name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Galsworthy's Forsyte novels the patriarch carries the prefix meaning elder to set him apart from his junior namesakes.

parts.note: Milton's Paradise Regained speaks of 'the olive grove' of Plato's school outside Athens

explanation.surface: It reads like the name of a suburban district with a street called Milton Grove.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a street address; Milton wrote of 'the olive grove of' Plato's school, the Athenian garden whose name now means the academic world.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato's school was in a grove near Athens, which Milton names; the word now stands for the university world.

clue.text: Gaps for a single girl in, say, point d'Alençon

indicators.note: the girl's name is placed in the fabric word

parts.note: point d'Alençon is a French needle lace
Una is a girl's name, and Latin una means one

explanation.surface: A lacemaker leaves holes in an expensive French lace for one young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the French needle lace as an example of the fabric; Una is a girl's name and also Latin for one, so 'a single girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacunae are missing portions or blanks, as in a text or manuscript.

clue.text: Aunt Dora's MS reveals a prominent forecaster

indicators.note: the letters of the aunt's name and manuscript are rearranged to reveal a hidden name

parts.note: the S of the possessive is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: An aunt's manuscript discloses the identity of a famous prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reveals' rearranges AUNT DORAS MS; MS is the usual short form of manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth-century French seer is famous for his rhyming prophecies.

indicators.note: read as a swap, the word sale exchanged for another arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Grazing land is on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals swapping SALE's letters around; the surface is an estate agent's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a grassy meadow, so the plural names grazing fields.

clue.text: Caterer is liable to be the ambitious type

indicators.note: the caterer's letters plus is are liable to become something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A catering worker is said to be a go-getter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liable to be' rearranges CATERER IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chiefly concerned with getting ahead in work is a social climber at the office.

parts.note: in law, the party to whom a wreck or other property is formally given up, such as an insurer

explanation.surface: A lawful collector of shipwrecks.
explanation.walkthrough: In marine insurance law the owner can give up a wreck to the insurer, who becomes the person it is relinquished to.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal term for the party to whom property is relinquished, typically an insurer taking over a wrecked ship.

parts.note: a nutritionist's A, B and C are lettered dietary nutrients rather than basics

explanation.surface: The basics of nutrition science.
explanation.walkthrough: ABC reads as 'the basics', but the letters are the names of essential nutrients A, B and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential nutrients are labelled A, B, C and so on, so a nutritionist's alphabet is these.

clue.text: Doc's with the girls, so sweet

parts.note: MO is the medical officer, a doctor
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A doctor spends time with the young women, and it is all very charming.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (medical officer) is a common abbreviation; 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is a sweet syrup made in sugar refining, so it is literally sugary.

clue.text: Miner's holding the busybodies who demand their rights

parts.note: a miner stakes a claim, the plot he holds
ants are emblematic busy workers

explanation.surface: A miner keeps hold of nosey parkers who insist on their entitlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' looks like a containment signal, but 'Miner's holding' is CLAIM, the staked plot.
explanation.definitionFit: People who assert a right to something, such as benefits or a title, put in demands for it.

indicators.note: turn tells you the word for about is turned round

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: Someone is told to turn round and leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' flips RE (about) to ER, followed by GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for therefore is used to mark a conclusion.

clue.text: The wonder is the poet has lost a pound

indicators.note: the poet's name loses a letter

parts.note: Andrew Marvell was a seventeenth-century English poet
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: A remarkable thing: the poet is a pound down.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Marvell, who wrote 'To His Coy Mistress', loses one L, the pound sign's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel is something astonishing, a thing to be wondered at.

clue.text: Was held up, but track now completed

parts.note: a way is a path or track
a track or railway that is laid is finished

explanation.surface: Someone was delayed, though the railway line has now been finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was' and 'but' are link words; a track is laid when it is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To waylay is to stop someone en route, often with an ambush, so held up on the road.

parts.note: top brass are high officers, but brazen hats point to bold-hatted ladies who are wholly female

explanation.surface: A claim that the senior officers are rather girly.
explanation.walkthrough: Brasshats means senior army officers; read as wearers of showy hats, the people who are wholly feminine are the female sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Being decidedly feminine is to be female adults.

clue.text: Many praise one article by her

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
to laud is to praise
I is the Roman numeral for one
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Lots of people commend a single newspaper piece she wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' is the definition, asking for a woman's name; C, LAUD, I and A sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name answers a clue that just says 'her'.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the two words terrific orgies

explanation.surface: A Welsh pet turns up at some wild parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the answer as lying inside 'terrifiC ORGIes'; Cymric means Welsh, and this short-legged dog is the Pembroke or Cardigan breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The short-legged herding dog originates in Wales and is a much-loved breed there.

clue.text: Appropriately involved in more sin is he ?

definitions.text: Appropriately involved in more sin is he ?

indicators.note: the words more sin is are involved, that is tangled, giving a rearranged order

explanation.surface: A preacher is supposedly mixed up in extra wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriately involved' rearranges MORE SIN IS; the whole clue describes a mission preacher, who is fittingly involved with sinners.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission preacher works among sinners, so is involved with sin in the course of his calling.

clue.text: " Our lives would grow together In —-or singing weather " (Swinburne)

definitions.text: " Our lives would grow together In —-or singing weather " (Swinburne)

parts.words: " Our lives would grow together In —-or singing weather " (Swinburne)
parts.note: lines from Swinburne's A Match, where the missing word is the opposite of singing, meaning mournful

explanation.surface: A quotation from Swinburne about two lives growing together.
explanation.walkthrough: Swinburne's poem A Match pairs a mournful word with 'singing weather'.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinburne's line contrasts singing weather with a mournful one.

definitions.meaning: to vamp is to patch up or repair
a vamp is a seductive woman who exploits men

explanation.surface: Women of dubious motives are called inconsistent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patchy' stands for the verb sense 'patches up', as a cobbler vamps old shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: To vamp is to patch up old shoes; a seductress who preys on men is also so called.

parts.note: Genesis says Cain went to dwell in a land east of Eden, and a penniless fugitive drifts there

explanation.surface: Where the banished Cain went, without a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis 4:16 sends Cain to a land east of Eden; also the land of sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis names the place east of Eden where Cain went after murdering Abel.

parts.note: read as fussy people, but meaning experts who concentrate on one particular field

explanation.surface: A remark that professionals are rather fussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'particular' suggests fussy; here it means confined to one narrow field.
explanation.definitionFit: Experts concentrating on one narrow area are those whose work is particular to it.
